q: Disintegration of measure: if π: (X,μ) → (Y,ν) is a measurable map with π_*μ = ν, then μ disintegrates as μ = ∫ μ_y dν(y) where each μ_y is:
opts: A probability measure on the fiber π⁻¹(y)
A measure on X equal to μ
exp: Disintegration: under mild regularity (e.g., standard Borel spaces), μ = ∫_Y μ_y dν(y) with μ_y supported on π⁻¹(y) and ∫ f dμ = ∫_Y (∫ f dμ_y) dν(y). This is the measure-theoretic analogue of conditional distributions.
